remaining_concerns: No genuinely new admissible evidence was provided; the Actor mainly reframed the same record more narrowly.
The policy requires admissible evidence of a material unresolved risk to support rejection, and that materiality bridge is still not documented in the record.
BPROC-006-E supports withholding approval pending follow-up if storage controls remained unresolved more directly than it supports outright rejection.
BPROC-006-C and BPROC-006-D are expressly the kinds of issues the policy treats as grounds for follow-up or escalation, not reject-level proof by themselves.
BPROC-006-B is only weak supplemental support because prior performance was mixed and limited.
final_rationale: The verdict does not change because the Actor supplied no new admissible evidence. The response appropriately narrows the rationale and concedes that the record does not prove a reject-level control failure, but that is a reinterpretation of the same evidence, not new support for the original compliance predicate. That narrower framing reduces overclaiming, yet it does not resolve the core audit concern: the admissible record still shows unresolved diligence questions and approval-readiness concerns more clearly than it shows a documented material unresolved risk sufficient to justify rejection under the stated policy. The distinction matters. A caveated statement that the vendor was not clearly approval-ready is more defensible than a statement that rejection was compliant, but it is not enough to convert the rejection decision itself into compliant or compliant_with_caveats without a contemporaneous materiality basis tying the unresolved issues to the reject threshold.
